description: A #meta blueprint that tiles one small room across a single floor with shift(). The meta references the #dig blueprint /quarters_unit four times: once at the cursor
column4: and shift(4 4) to drop three more copies. Each unit is 3 tiles wide and tall
column5: so a shift of 4 leaves a one tile undug wall between neighbours
column6: laying a 2x2 block of separate rooms in one pass. shift(dx dy) offsets every tile of the referenced blueprint: +x moves right
column10: and the comma is optional so shift(4 0) sits in one CSV cell without splitting. This is the corpus's first shift() example and its first in-floor meta tiling: where meta-residential-tower.csv uses repeat(down 5) to stack a floor down the Z-axis
column11: this spreads a room across one floor. The sibling marker transform(rotcw rotccw fliph flipv) rotates or flips a referenced blueprint instead of moving it (rotating a #build blueprint also turns its direction-sensitive machinery)
column12: and if both markers are on one reference the shift is applied after all transforms. Carve a corridor of your own to link the four rooms
column13: or widen the shift to leave room for one.
